LOCATION: kitchen shelf where everything earned its keeping
patched coat with pockets that outlasted the wedding it was bought for
root cellar where the jars remember which summer
threshold where the walker stops to set the bag down
pantry with handwriting on every label and none of it the same hand
return-path that got longer each time the walker picked something up
the hollow under the stairs where the bag finally rests
gathering-field where the harvest has teeth if you thank it wrong
potter's window where the seams show and nothing leaks
bottom of the pouch where the oldest seed is
hearth with a sling draped over the chair like punctuation
ANTAGONIST: the spear-thinker who mistakes holding for hoarding
the editor who cuts every song to 3:18 and calls it done
the hero's climax that needs everything else thrown away
the tidy hand that wants the bag empty before nightfall
the story-grammar that demands resolution at the outer layer
the quiet voice that says 'you don't need this one' about the thing you'll need in November
the appraiser who weighs the bag without smelling it
MACGUFFIN: a seed with next summer already folded inside it
a busted yo-yo called 'how time flies when you stop counting'
a stone that remembers which pocket held it through the cold year
the medicine bundle nobody opens but everybody reaches for
the line you wrote down three weeks before you knew you'd need it
the marble that was once traded for the moon and came back warmer
a scrap of cloth worn soft by the hand of someone who was not the owner
THREAT: the seam splits at the bottom and the oldest seed is the one that falls
the walker learns to throw away and forgets what gathering was for
the bag is called a burden by someone who never picked up anything
the hero arrives and demands the bag resolve into a spear
the tidy hand empties the bag on the floor and calls it clarity
the song is cut to 3:18 and the eight-minute version is thrown out
the label peels off and the summer is lost
CHARACTER: the old woman with pockets full of seeds and no particular plan
the trickster who traded the moon for marbles and kept the marbles
the keeper who never sorted, only held
the walker who picked up one more thing every mile and still arrived on time
the potter whose seams are crooked and whose vessels still hold
the small child with a sling full of rocks and a name for each one
the ghost of the gatherer who taught the spear-thinker to notice the bag
